author: single_bar_shape_b
note: Predicates 12-18: long-wick, marubozu, belt-hold, spinning-top. All read ONLY bars[0]; RequiredBars=3 (default), so the two filler bars at index 1-2 are inert and cannot create or destroy any pattern. Bars are [open, high, low, close, tick_volume]; bars[0] is the reference (most recently closed) bar. Note the identity range = body + upper_wick + lower_wick holds for every candle.

fixtures.rationale: A long lower wick means price was driven far below the body and rejected, leaving a long shadow beneath. Body sits at the top: low 97, body bottom 100, so the lower shadow is 3.0 of a 3.5 range (86%), the classic downside-rejection candle.
The mirror shape: the long shadow is on the WRONG (upper) side. Body sits at the bottom, lower wick only 0.1 of a 3.1 range (3%). This is upside rejection, not a long lower wick, and must not fire.
A lower shadow exists but is not long: lower wick 0.8 of a 1.8 range = 44%, less than the body/upper portion. A candle whose lower wick is under half the range is not read as a long-lower-wick bar.
Lower wick 1.1 on range 2.0 = 55%, inside (above) the 50%-of-range floor. Only the lower-wick value is tuned; body and upper wick stay valid so this isolates the single threshold.
Lower wick 0.9 on range 2.0 = 45%, outside (below) the 50% floor. One value changed from the inside case; the ~5% gap on each side keeps the pair clear of float-equality noise.

A long upper wick means price was pushed far above the body and rejected. Body sits at the bottom (body top 100.2, high 103), so the upper shadow is 2.8 of a 3.2 range (88%), the classic upside-rejection candle.
The mirror shape: the long shadow is on the lower side. Body sits near the top, upper wick only 0.2 of a 3.2 range (6%). This is downside rejection, not a long upper wick, and must not fire.
An upper shadow exists but is not long: upper wick 0.8 of a 1.9 range = 42%, under half the range. Not a long-upper-wick bar.
Upper wick 1.1 on range 2.0 = 55%, inside (above) the 50%-of-range floor. Body top is 99.9, high 101; only the upper-wick value is tuned so the fixture isolates the threshold.
Upper wick 0.9 on range 2.0 = 45%, outside (below) the 50% floor. One value changed from the inside case, ~5% margin each side to avoid float-equality issues.
A bullish marubozu opens at its low and closes at its high with no shadows: pure buying all session. Open 100 = low, close 105 = high, body 5.0 = 100% of the 5.0 range, bullish.
A full-body candle but BEARISH (open 105 = high, close 100 = low). This is a bear marubozu; the bull variant must not fire on a down candle. Isolates the direction clause.
Bullish but the body is tiny relative to the range: body 1.0 on a 6.0 range = 17%, with long shadows. A marubozu is nearly all body, so this fails. Isolates the body-fraction clause.

Body 19.6 on range 20.0 = 98%, inside (above) the 95%-of-range body floor. Tiny 0.2 wicks each side; bullish. The narrow 95-100% band means margin above the floor is bounded, but 3 points of range far exceeds float noise.
Body 18.0 on range 20.0 = 90%, outside (below) the 95% floor. Still clearly bullish; only the body/wick split changed from the inside case.
A bearish marubozu opens at its high and closes at its low with no shadows: pure selling all session. Open 105 = high, close 100 = low, body 5.0 = 100% of the 5.0 range, bearish.
A full-body candle but BULLISH (open 100 = low, close 105 = high). This is a bull marubozu; the bear variant must not fire on an up candle. Isolates the direction clause.
Bearish but body is tiny: body 1.0 on a 6.0 range = 17%, with long shadows. Not a marubozu. Isolates the body-fraction clause.
Body 19.6 on range 20.0 = 98%, inside (above) the 95% body floor. Tiny 0.2 wicks each side; bearish (open 119.8 > close 100.2).
Body 18.0 on range 20.0 = 90%, outside (below) the 95% floor. Still clearly bearish; only the body/wick split changed from the inside case.
A bullish belt-hold opens at the session low (no lower shadow) and closes far up. Open 100 = low so lower wick 0, body 7.0 = 70% of the 10.0 range, a small 3.0 upper wick, bullish.

Bullish with a strong body but it does NOT open at the low: lower wick 3.0 of a 10.0 range = 30%. Belt-hold requires opening at the extreme, so a substantial lower shadow disqualifies it. Isolates the lower-wick clause.

Bullish and opens at the low (lower wick 0) but the body is weak: 2.0 of a 10.0 range = 20%, with a huge 8.0 upper wick. A belt-hold needs a decisive body; this is closer to a long-upper-wick reversal. Isolates the body clause.
A bearish belt-hold-bear shape (opens at high 110, closes down at 103). The bull variant requires an up candle, so a down candle must not fire it regardless of body strength.
Lower wick 0.3 on range 10.0 = 3%, inside (under) the 5%-of-range lower-wick ceiling. Body 6.5 = 65% stays comfortably above its own floor so this isolates the lower-wick threshold.
Lower wick 0.7 on range 10.0 = 7%, outside (over) the 5% ceiling. Body still 65%; only the lower-wick value changed from the inside case.
Body 6.3 on range 10.0 = 63%, inside (above) the 60%-of-range body floor. Opens at the low (lower wick 0) so only the body value is under test.
Body 5.7 on range 10.0 = 57%, outside (below) the 60% floor. Opens at the low so the lower-wick clause still passes; only the body changed from the inside case.
A bearish belt-hold opens at the session high (no upper shadow) and closes far down. Open 110 = high so upper wick 0, body 7.0 = 70% of the 10.0 range, a small 3.0 lower wick, bearish.

Bearish with a strong body but it does NOT open at the high: upper wick 3.0 of an 11.0 range = 27%. Belt-hold requires opening at the extreme, so a substantial upper shadow disqualifies it. Isolates the upper-wick clause.
Bearish and opens at the high (upper wick 0) but the body is weak: 2.0 of a 10.0 range = 20%, with a huge 8.0 lower wick. Not a decisive belt-hold. Isolates the body clause.
A bullish full-body candle (open 100 = low, close 104 = high, upper wick 0). The bear variant requires a down candle, so an up candle must not fire it regardless of body strength.
Upper wick 0.3 on range 10.0 = 3%, inside (under) the 5%-of-range upper-wick ceiling. Body 6.5 = 65% stays above its floor so this isolates the upper-wick threshold.
Upper wick 0.7 on range 10.0 = 7%, outside (over) the 5% ceiling. Body still 65%; only the upper-wick value changed from the inside case.
Body 6.3 on range 10.0 = 63%, inside (above) the 60%-of-range body floor. Opens at the high (upper wick 0) so only the body value is under test.
Body 5.7 on range 10.0 = 57%, outside (below) the 60% floor. Opens at the high so the upper-wick clause still passes; only the body changed from the inside case.

A spinning top is indecision: a small central body flanked by comparable wicks on both sides. Body 2.8 = 28% of the 10.0 range, upper wick 3.6 = 36%, lower wick 3.6 = 36%. Body modest, both shadows long: textbook spinning top.

Not indecision but conviction: body 6.0 = 60% of the 10.0 range with only 2.0 (20%) wicks each side. A body that dominates the range is a directional candle, not a spinning top. Attacks the body-ceiling meaning.

Body 0.5 = 5% of the 10.0 range with 4.75 (47.5%) wicks each side: open and close are almost equal. That is a doji / long-legged doji, not a spinning top, which needs a small but real body. Attacks the body-floor meaning.

Body 2.8 = 28% sits in the band and the lower wick is 6.7 (67%), but the upper wick is only 0.5 = 5%. A spinning top needs indecision on BOTH sides; a single dominant shadow makes this a hammer-like bar. Isolates the upper-wick clause.

Body 2.8 = 28% sits in the band and the upper wick is 6.7 (67%), but the lower wick is only 0.5 = 5%. Wicks must flank both sides; a single dominant upper shadow makes this an inverted-hammer-like bar. Isolates the lower-wick clause.
Body 2.2 on range 10.0 = 22%, inside (above) the 20% body floor. Both wicks 3.9 = 39% stay well above their 25% floors, so this isolates the body-floor edge alone.
Body 1.8 on range 10.0 = 18%, outside (below) the 20% body floor. Wicks 4.1 = 41% each still valid; only the body shrank from the inside case, isolating the floor.
Body 3.3 on range 10.0 = 33%, inside (below) the 35% body ceiling. Both wicks 3.35 = 33.5% stay above their floors, isolating the body-ceiling edge.
Body 3.7 on range 10.0 = 37%, outside (above) the 35% body ceiling. Wicks 3.15 = 31.5% each still valid; only the body grew from the inside case.
Upper wick 2.7 on range 10.0 = 27%, inside (above) the 25% upper-wick floor. Body 2.8 = 28% and lower wick 4.5 = 45% stay valid, isolating the upper-wick floor.
Upper wick 2.3 on range 10.0 = 23%, outside (below) the 25% upper-wick floor. Body 2.8 = 28% and lower wick 4.9 = 49% still valid; only the upper wick shrank from the inside case.
Lower wick 2.7 on range 10.0 = 27%, inside (above) the 25% lower-wick floor. Body 2.8 = 28% and upper wick 4.5 = 45% stay valid, isolating the lower-wick floor.
Lower wick 2.3 on range 10.0 = 23%, outside (below) the 25% lower-wick floor. Body 2.8 = 28% and upper wick 4.9 = 49% still valid; only the lower wick shrank from the inside case.
